body.statement: For a resolution partition \(\mathscr Q\), prove or disprove the information-saturation relation \(\mathcal B(w_n)\asymp n\) as \(n\to\infty\), where \(w_n=\inf\{w>0:\mathcal B(w)\le n\}\) and no power law is imposed. Establish weak duality \(\mathcal D(w)\le\mathcal B(w)\), determine whether equality of values holds under the stated Hölder--margin alternative sets without assuming dual attainment, and characterize any failure caused by discontinuities or inactive cells. Then determine whether, with \(n=T\), the handle \(\mathsf H_{T,\rho}\) can turn the resulting arm-specific cell quotas into one predictable design and one connected interval that uniformly satisfy participant-welfare loss at most \(\rho\), \(1-\delta\) honesty, and expected width of order \(w_n\) while respecting stochastic context-arrival capacities.
body.justification: The semi-infinite covering program exposes the exact local information demand before asking whether random context arrivals and gap-priced exploration can realize it.
body.gap: HuKallusMao2022SmoothContextualBandits controls regret under selective exploration, LiShiSimchiLevi2024PrivateAdaptiveDesign balances finite strata, and BibautEtAl2021PostContextualBanditInference stabilizes inference under supplied propensities; none proves primal saturation, dual value equality, and sequential quota realization for target-separating continuous-context alternatives under a hard welfare budget.
body.consumer: A positive saturation and realization result supplies the implementable upper half of the frontier; a failure identifies whether alternative-set geometry, context capacity, or participant cost creates an additional width branch.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove right closedness and a uniform no-overshoot bound for the generalized inverse \(w_n\), and construct from the quotas an actual predictable design plus connected interval obeying random context-arrival capacities and the welfare budget.
obligation.obstruction: Fixed-\(w\) primal--dual value equality does not control discontinuities of \(w\mapsto\mathcal B(w)\). The frozen handle \(\mathsf H_{T,\rho}\) is descriptive prose: it specifies neither assignment kernels nor interval endpoints, and the allocation program has no stochastic cell-capacity or welfare-price constraint. Those missing maps and inequalities cannot be inferred from the definition.
obligation.attempted: Reduced every active-cell program to a two-dimensional zero-sum game, proved weak duality, derived equality of primal and measure-dual values through finite-dimensional convex separation, and analyzed the generalized inverse. This isolates the remaining step as continuity/jump control plus sequential quota realization, not duality.
obligation.partial_result:
Weak duality does follow from the frozen programs.  If \(z\) is primal feasible and \(\lambda_{\mathsf Q}\) is dual feasible, then for every active cell
\[
\kappa_\delta\lambda_{\mathsf Q}(\mathcal S_{\mathsf Q}(w))
\leq\int\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}z_{\mathsf Q,a}k_{\mathsf Q,a}(s)\,d\lambda_{\mathsf Q}(s)
\leq\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}z_{\mathsf Q,a}.
\]
Summing and taking the supremum and infimum gives \(\mathcal D(w)\leq\mathcal B(w)\).

There is also value equality at every fixed \(w>0\), without dual attainment, provided the phrase ``finite nonnegative measures'' includes finite atomic measures.  For one active cell put
\[
K=\{(k_{\mathsf Q,0}(s),k_{\mathsf Q,1}(s)):s\in\mathcal S_{\mathsf Q}(w)\},
\quad
v=\sup_{u\in\Delta_2}\inf_{k\in K}u\cdot k.
\]
Writing a nonzero primal vector as \(z=c u\), where \(c=z_0+z_1\) and \(u\in\Delta_2\), shows that the cellwise primal value is \(\kappa_\delta/v\), with the usual value \(+\infty\) when \(v=0\).  The coefficients are bounded by \(2M^2/\sigma^2\).  Finite-dimensional separation of the compact convex set \(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}K\) from lower coordinate boxes gives
\[
v=\inf_{\nu\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{fin}}(K)}
\max_{a\in\mathcal A}\int k_a\,d\nu(k).
\]
Scaling an approximating finite-support probability \(\nu\) into a dual measure shows that the dual cell value is the same \(\kappa_\delta/v\).  The programs separate over the finitely many active cells, hence \(\mathcal D(w)=\mathcal B(w)\).

The remaining saturation and sequential-realization assertions do not follow from this fixed-\(w\) duality.  The map \(w\mapsto\mathcal B(w)\) is nonincreasing, but its generalized inverse only implies
\[
\mathcal B(w_n-)\geq n.
\]
To infer \(\mathcal B(w_n)\leq n\) one needs right closedness at \(w_n\); to infer a constant lower multiple of \(n\) one additionally needs a uniform bound on the downward jump at \(w_n\); and one needs \(w_n>0\) because \(\mathcal B\) was defined only for \(w>0\).  None of these properties is stated or proved for the nonconvex H\"older--margin alternative sets.  Finally, the handle does not specify predictable kernels, quota truncation under random cell arrivals, interval endpoints, or a coverage calculation, so it is not yet a sample-to-output map to which welfare or honesty can be applied.
